0.0.n: Combines with つ and 目 to label the third item.

0.1.n: A general counting suffix used here with 3.

0.2.n: Added after a count to show position in a sequence.

0.7.n: Links the placeholder 〇〇 to its Japanese equivalent.

0.8.n: Refers here to the Japanese word or expression for 〇〇.

0.9.n: Marks the Japanese equivalent of 〇〇 as what the question is about.

0.10.n: Read as なん before です in this question.

0.12.n: Placed at the end to turn the sentence into a question.

0.15.n: Marks the preceding question as the words someone would ask.

0.16.n: Negative form of 聞ける, the ability form of 聞く; here 聞く refers to asking, not listening.

0.17.n: The phrase before 人 describes which people; Japanese does not require a plural ending.

1.0.n: Points back to the point being discussed.

1.1.n: Marks これ as the topic of the sentence.

1.2.n: Refers to the language people have started learning.

1.3.n: Marks 日本語 as what people have begun studying.

1.4.n: Past form of 始める, describing the people who have begun learning Japanese.

1.5.n: Modified by 日本語を始めた, identifying those who have started learning Japanese.

1.6.n: Marks the first group for whom this point is important.

1.7.n: Paired with the later も to include both groups.

1.9.n: Indicates that these speakers have reached this level by now.

1.10.n: Describes a fairly high degree of speaking ability.

1.11.n: Ability form of 話す, describing what these people are able to do.

1.12.n: Modified by もう結構話せる, identifying those with established speaking ability.

1.13.n: Marks the second group for whom this point is important.

1.14.n: Includes this second group alongside beginners.

1.15.n: Used with な before a noun to describe something that matters.

1.16.n: Connects 大切 to the noun こと it describes.

1.17.n: Refers to an abstract point or practice, not a physical object.

2.1.n: Marks 日本語 as what the speaker is practicing.

2.2.n: 練習する becomes 練習している to describe an activity in progress.

2.3.n: The preceding phrase describes the time during which the advice applies.

2.4.n: Sets practicing time as the situation being discussed.

2.6.n: Encourages following the advice to the extent one can.

2.7.n: Names the language recommended for speaking.

2.8.n: Limits the language used to Japanese.

2.9.n: Marks the language used as the means of speaking.

2.10.n: Plain form of 話す, followed by の to treat the action as a thing.

2.11.n: Turns 話す into a noun-like phrase that can be described as good.

2.12.n: Marks the act of speaking only Japanese as what is good.

2.13.n: Expresses a recommendation here rather than simply judging quality.

2.14.n: Shortened form of の in のです, giving the advice an explanatory tone.

2.16.n: Draws the listener's attention to advice the speaker wants them to know.

0.lit: Third item: people who cannot ask, “As for the Japanese of 〇〇, what is it?”
0.tip: 聞けない describes inability to ask, while と marks the exact question being quoted.

1.lit: This is an important thing both for people who started Japanese and for people who already can speak quite well.
1.tip: The repeated にも includes both groups: this matters for beginners and more capable speakers alike.

2.lit: When practicing Japanese, speaking only in Japanese as much as possible is good, you know.
2.tip: A verb followed by のがいい presents that action as a good choice or recommendation.
